name: API - Unrestricted Resource Consumption (API4:2023)
command: dd if=/dev/urandom of=big.pdf bs=1M count=30   # upload via the vulnerable endpoint - no size/type/rate limit
description: An API that doesn't limit file size, file type, or request rate on an upload endpoint (CWE-400) lets an attacker exhaust disk/bandwidth (DoS + financial cost), bypass extension checks to upload executables, and - when files land in a publicly served path (e.g. ASP.NET Core wwwroot) - host malware or stage a payload for social-engineering RCE.

examples.label: Get your supplier-company / object ID first
Generate a 30 MB junk 'PDF' (no size limit -> storage DoS)
Generate an .exe (no type validation -> executable upload)
Download it back from the public wwwroot path

notes: Three failures compound here: (1) no file-size cap -> repeat uploads exhaust disk = DoS + cloud-storage cost; (2) no file-type/extension validation -> upload a real msfvenom .exe instead of a PDF; (3) ASP.NET Core serves /wwwroot statically by default, so uploaded files are publicly downloadable - the API becomes free malware hosting, and a socially-engineered admin opening the .exe yields RCE. Enumerating filenames under wwwroot can also expose other customers' documents. The module drives the upload via the API UI/Postman; the multipart curl equivalent is: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" -F "file=@reverse-shell.exe" -F "companyId=<id>" http://<ip>:<port>/api/v1/supplier-companies/certificates-of-incorporation.

recommended.note: Where this sits in the OWASP API Top 10.
Enumerate other objects/files once you can read wwwroot.

defense.prerequisites: Authenticated API user with access to an upload endpoint that lacks size/type/rate controls; uploaded files served from a public path.
defense.why_it_works: The endpoint saves user-supplied files without validating size, extension/content-type, or request rate, and the storage directory is web-served, so arbitrary bytes and executables become publicly retrievable.
defense.misconfiguration: No max-file-size, no MIME/extension allowlist, no rate limiting/quota on the upload endpoint; files stored inside the web root (ASP.NET Core wwwroot served statically by default).
defense.impact: Denial of service via disk/bandwidth exhaustion and cloud cost; malware hosting on a trusted domain; executable delivery leading to RCE if an admin runs it; exposure of other users' uploaded documents.
defense.detection: Spikes in upload volume/size from one token/IP; uploads with non-document extensions; repeated identical large uploads; static requests to wwwroot upload paths; storage-utilization alarms.
defense.artifacts: Oversized/executable files under the upload dir (e.g. wwwroot/...); app logs of large multipart POSTs; egress logs of the public download.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web sourcetype=access_combined uri_path="*/api/*"
| stats count by clientip, bin(_time, 1m)
| where count>500
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem has "/api/"
| summarize reqs=count() by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where reqs > 500
| sort by reqs desc
// unrestricted resource consumption (API rate abuse / large page sizes)
defense.sigma_rules: web_api_rate_abuse (unbounded request volume to an API)
defense.vulnerable_config:
// ASP.NET Core: app.UseStaticFiles();  // wwwroot public
// upload endpoint: no [RequestSizeLimit], no extension/MIME check, no rate limit
defense.prevention: Cap file size and total quota per user; allowlist content types and verify magic bytes; rate-limit uploads; store files outside the web root and serve through an authorization check; scan uploads with AV. [MITRE M1041, M1037, M1013]
defense.evasion: Stay under obvious size/volume thresholds; use a valid PDF magic-byte header on an executable-laden file; spread uploads across time to dodge rate alarms.
defense.code_review:
RED FLAGS (source): file saved using client-supplied name/extension; MIME trusted from the request.
  move_uploaded_file(..., $_FILES['f']['name'])  |  extension blacklist  |  type check on $_FILES['f']['type'] (client-controlled)
GREP:  grep -rniE "move_uploaded_file|\$_FILES|multer|formidable|MultipartFile|SaveAs\(" .
SAFE:  extension ALLOWLIST + magic-byte MIME (finfo/mime_content_type), server-generated random filename, store outside webroot in a no-execute dir.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review IIS Web Server logs, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response
